# Paragraph-style numbering bindings

Original XML/OPC controls generated by `tools/numbering_style_selection_fixture.py`.
No corpus content, third-party engine, artwork or font files are included.
The source is covered by the repository license. Reference-generated PDF/PNG files
are native reference output from these original controls, not renderer output.

The 34 cases distinguish explicit/inherited/omitted levels, stale links,
ancestor links, level overrides, direct level-only and numId declarations,
explicit cancellation, and reciprocal ownership of a level. Cases also separate
another instance of the same abstract list from a different abstract definition,
and direct level-only overrides entering/leaving an owned level. A stale
`pStyle` alone does not suppress a marker.

The reference application produced `native.pdf` and the COM observations in
`native.json`, using `tools/capture-numbering-style-selection.ps1`. The independent
`tools/record_numbering_style_bindings.py` confirms every marker against the
PDF and records all text/marker origins. `reference.json` binds the source,
case inventory, PDF and COM observations by SHA-256. The generator is deterministic.

ECMA-376 Part 1 §§17.3.1.19 (`numPr`), 17.9.3 (`ilvl`), and 17.9.23 (`pStyle`)
describe numbering selection. The reference application diverges from the rule that a paragraph
style's `ilvl` is ignored, as documented in
[MS-OI29500 §2.1.50](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/openspecs/office_standards/ms-oi29500/6a8f14ff-df90-4154-9bc9-e0e88ae5e641).
These controls establish the supported behavior; the implementation note does
not promise a universal resolution algorithm for contradictory declarations.

The reference application uses an explicit style level, otherwise level zero; it does not infer a
different level from a stale `pStyle`. When the inherited style's level
reciprocally belongs to another style in the same abstract list, numbering omits
the marker but keeps that inherited level's geometry. A direct level alone does
not change this result. A paragraph's explicit `numId` overrides the ownership
restriction. Explicit cancellation remains separate and removes numbering
geometry. Applying the owning style activates its marker.

Unit tests verify native markers, source hashes, style changes and exact undo.
Browser tests verify all native text/marker origins, list-button state, typing,
untouched package parts, undo and reopening. This is scoped evidence for these
rules, not certification of every possible conflicting numbering definition.
